title: Published per-entity document
description: Contract for the per-entity endpoints emitted by tools/build.py to v1/{dataset}/{id}.json. These are the DEEP surface: the canonical entity plus everything the build projects onto it, and for camps they are the only place the prose `note` on a program feature appears. Scope is deliberate: this schema pins the ENVELOPE and the PROJECTION - that `versions` is a non-empty ordered history, that lifecycle `events` are folded in under that exact key with resolved participants, and that `requirement_sets` lists the editions belonging to a subject. The interior of each `version` is already validated against its canonical schema (council/camp/merit-badge/...) by tools/validate_data.py before the build runs, so it is not restated here; what was previously unguarded, and is now, is the projection step - renaming `events`, dropping `requirement_sets`, or emitting an entity with no versions used to be a one-line edit no gate would catch. Fields are ADDITIVE-ONLY under v1, like every other published surface. The item shape is selected BY `kind`.

Version.description: One attribute snapshot. Half-open window: `valid_from` null means 'from the beginning of what we know', `valid_to` null means current. Exactly one version per entity may have valid_to null (enforced by tools/validate_data.py). Attribute fields beyond these are dataset-specific and validated against the canonical schema for that kind.

Event.description: A lifecycle event PROJECTED onto this entity from the dataset's _events.json. Stored once there, copied here for convenience: an entity carries every event it participates in, whichever role it plays.

requirement_sets.description: Ids of every requirement-set edition whose `subject` is this entity, oldest and newest alike - not just the one in force. Fetch v1/requirement-sets/{id}.json for the tree, or read the effective windows and `supersedes` chain to pick the edition that applied on a given date.

RequirementSetDocument.description: An effective-dated requirement document (merit badge or rank edition). Not a versioned entity: editions are immutable and chained by `supersedes`, so there are no `versions` and no `events`.

then.description: A document carrying verbatim official text MUST state its rights. Requirement text is © Scouting America and sits outside this dataset's CC licence; publishing it without the carve-out recorded on the document itself would misrepresent the licence.

TrainingRequirementDocument.description: One row of the TRAINED LEADER REQUIREMENTS chart: what an adult in this position, in this unit type, must complete to be Position Trained. Not a versioned entity - the chart is a single edition and the row has no identity apart from it. `registration_codes` is the join key a consumer already holds from my.scouting; `position_name` is display only and is printed with the source's own typos.

BadgeRankingDocument.description: One year of merit badge popularity ranks. Like a requirement-set it is a dated document, not a versioned entity, so it carries neither `versions` nor `events`. `metric` is pinned because the numbers are RANKS, not counts, and a consumer that mistook one for the other would draw volume conclusions the source never supports.
